subproblems.title: Smooth L¹-approximation of indicators of subsets of a ball
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let ℝⁿ = Euclid n carry Lebesgue measure L, let R, η ∈ ℝ with η > 0, and let P ⊆ ℝⁿ be a Borel set with P ⊆ B_R(0) (open ball). Then there is a C¹ function ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support, tsupport ψ ⊆ B_R(0), 0 ≤ ψ(z) ≤ 1 for all z, and ∫ |ψ − 1_P| dL < η.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (P : Set (Euclid n)) (R η : ℝ), MeasurableSet P → P ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) R → 0 < η → ∃ ψ : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ ∧ HasCompactSupport ψ ∧ tsupport ψ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) R ∧ (∀ z, 0 ≤ ψ z ∧ ψ z ≤ 1) ∧ ∫ z, |ψ z - P.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) z| < η
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 1, last sentence (the duality ‖f‖_{1,R} = sup{∫ fψ : ψ admissible}), where admissible smooth approximants of sgn f on B_R are needed. The parent produces them by mollifying sgn f and using a.e. convergence of mollifiers; that Mathlib theorem (ContDiffBump.ae_convolution_tendsto_right_of_locallyIntegrable) and ContDiffBump.normed are NOT in the frozen import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, so the approximants are produced here from regularity of Lebesgue measure and the smooth Urysohn lemma, which are in the closure. Notation: B_r := B_r(0), L := Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ.

1. Since P ⊆ B_R, L(P) ≤ L(B_R) < ∞.
2. (Inner regularity.) Lebesgue measure is inner regular on sets of finite measure with respect to compact sets, so there is a compact (hence closed, Borel) set K ⊆ P with L(P ∖ K) < η/2.
3. (Outer regularity at a compact set.) There is an open U ⊇ K with L(U) < L(K) + η/2. As K ⊆ U and L(K) < ∞, L(U ∖ K) = L(U) − L(K) < η/2.
4. K is closed and K ⊆ B_R; in the proper space ℝⁿ there is r' < R with K ⊆ B_{r'} (if K ≠ ∅ the norm attains a maximum m < R on the compact K and any r' ∈ (m, R) works; if K = ∅ take r' := R − 1).
5. s := U ∩ B_{r'} is open and K ⊆ s by 3 and 4. By the smooth Urysohn lemma in the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ (for an open s and a closed t ⊆ s there is a C^∞ function with values in [0, 1], support exactly s, and equal to 1 exactly on t), applied with t := K, there is a C^∞ (in particular C¹) ψ : ℝⁿ → [0, 1] with support ψ = s and ψ(z) = 1 ⟺ z ∈ K.
6. tsupport ψ = closure(s) ⊆ closedBall(0, r') ⊆ B_R because r' < R; closedBall(0, r') is compact, so ψ has compact support. Also 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1.
7. (Pointwise domination.) For every z: |ψ(z) − 1_P(z)| ≤ 1_{P∖K}(z) + 1_{s∖K}(z). Cases: (a) z ∈ K: ψ(z) = 1 = 1_P(z) (K ⊆ P), the left side is 0 and the right side is ≥ 0. (b) z ∈ P ∖ K: the left side is |ψ(z) − 1| ≤ 1 = 1_{P∖K}(z). (c) z ∉ P and z ∈ s: then z ∉ K and the left side is ψ(z) ≤ 1 = 1_{s∖K}(z). (d) z ∉ P and z ∉ s: ψ(z) = 0 because support ψ = s, so the left side is 0.
8. P ∖ K and s ∖ K are Borel with L(P ∖ K) < η/2 and L(s ∖ K) ≤ L(U ∖ K) < η/2 (s ∖ K ⊆ U ∖ K); their indicators are integrable. Integrating 7 (the left side is ≥ 0): ∫ |ψ − 1_P| dL ≤ L(P ∖ K) + L(s ∖ K) < η/2 + η/2 = η. ∎

subproblems.title: L¹ norm on a ball is bounded by testing against C¹ functions (bounded integrands)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, R, A, M ∈ ℝ, and let f : ℝⁿ → ℝ be Borel with |f(z)| ≤ M for all z. Suppose ∫ f φ dL ≤ A for every C¹ function φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) and |φ(z)| ≤ 1 for all z. Then ∫_{B_R(0)} |f| dL ≤ A.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Euclid n → ℝ) (R A M : ℝ), Measurable f → (∀ z, |f z| ≤ M) → (∀ φ : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) R → (∀ z, |φ z| ≤ 1) → ∫ z, f z * φ z ≤ A) → ∫ z in ball (0 : Euclid n) R, |f z| ≤ A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 1, last sentence ('‖f‖_{1,R} = sup{∫ fψ : ψ as above} for f ∈ L¹_loc …'), specialized to bounded Borel f, which is the only case used (f = 1_F − 1_F(· − w) in translation_l1). The admissible approximants of sgn f come from sibling smooth_indicator_approx; boundedness of f replaces the parent's a.e.-convergence/dominated-convergence step. Notation: B_R := B_R(0).

1. M ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0. Let P := {z : f(z) > 0} ∩ B_R and N := {z : f(z) < 0} ∩ B_R; both are Borel subsets of B_R. Put g := 1_P − 1_N.
2. f·g = 1_{B_R}·|f| pointwise: for z ∉ B_R, z ∉ P ∪ N and both sides vanish; for z ∈ B_R, if f(z) > 0 then g(z) = 1 and f g = f = |f|; if f(z) < 0 then g(z) = −1 and f g = −f = |f|; if f(z) = 0 both sides vanish. Hence ∫_{B_R} |f| dL = ∫ f g dL, and f g is integrable (Borel, bounded by M, zero outside B_R, L(B_R) < ∞).
3. Let η > 0 and η' := η / (2(M + 1)) > 0. Apply smooth_indicator_approx to P and to N (radius R, accuracy η'): there are C¹ functions ψ_P, ψ_N with compact support, tsupport ⊆ B_R, values in [0, 1], ∫ |ψ_P − 1_P| < η' and ∫ |ψ_N − 1_N| < η'.
4. φ := ψ_P − ψ_N is C¹, has compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ tsupport ψ_P ∪ tsupport ψ_N ⊆ B_R, and |φ| ≤ 1 (difference of two numbers in [0, 1]). By hypothesis ∫ f φ ≤ A; f φ is integrable (φ continuous with compact support, f bounded Borel).
5. Pointwise: f g − f φ = f·((1_P − ψ_P) − (1_N − ψ_N)) ≤ |f|·(|ψ_P − 1_P| + |ψ_N − 1_N|) ≤ M·(|ψ_P − 1_P| + |ψ_N − 1_N|). The functions |ψ_P − 1_P|, |ψ_N − 1_N| are integrable (continuous compactly supported function minus the indicator of a finite-measure Borel set). Integrating: ∫ f g − ∫ f φ ≤ M·S with S := ∫ |ψ_P − 1_P| + ∫ |ψ_N − 1_N|, and 0 ≤ S < 2η'.
6. Since S ≥ 0, M·S ≤ (M + 1)·S < (M + 1)·2η' = η. Therefore ∫_{B_R} |f| = ∫ f g < ∫ f φ + η ≤ A + η.
7. As η > 0 is arbitrary, ∫_{B_R} |f| dL ≤ A. (No case distinction on R is needed: for R ≤ 0, P = N = ∅ and the same computation applies.) ∎

subproblems.title: Perimeter bound controls translation differences of C¹ test functions
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, F ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel, R, C ∈ ℝ and w ∈ ℝⁿ. Assume ∫_F div g dL ≤ C for every C¹ vector field g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ B_{R+|w|}(0) and |g(z)| ≤ 1 for all z, where div g(z) := trace Dg(z). Then for every C¹ function φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) and |φ| ≤ 1: ∫_F (φ(z) − φ(z + w)) dz ≤ |w|·C.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Set (Euclid n)) (R C : ℝ) (w : Euclid n) (φ : Euclid n → ℝ), MeasurableSet F → (∀ g : Euclid n → Euclid n, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) (R + ‖w‖) → (∀ z, ‖g z‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ z in F, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g z : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid n) ≤ C) → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) R → (∀ z, |φ z| ≤ 1) → ∫ z in F, (φ z - φ (z + w)) ≤ ‖w‖ * C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 1: the identity ψ(x) − ψ(x − w) = ∫_0^1 ⟨∇ψ(x − tw), w⟩ dt = div_x((∫_0^1 ψ(x − tw) dt) w), and the application of the hypothesis to the field divided by its sup-norm bound. Here it is used for a single translation vector w, with the t-integral taken outside the divergence: d/dt ∫_F φ(z + tw) dz = −|w|·∫_F div G_t for the elementary fields G_t below, so no parametric vector field has to be differentiated. Notation: B_r := B_r(0), |·| the Euclidean norm, Dφ the derivative.

1. Applying the hypothesis to g = 0 (C¹, compact support, empty tsupport, |g| ≤ 1, div g = 0) gives 0 ≤ C. If w = 0 the left side is ∫_F 0 = 0 = |w|·C. From now on w ≠ 0, so |w| > 0.
2. (Elementary fields.) For t ∈ [0, 1] let G_t(z) := (−|w|⁻¹ φ(z + tw))·w.
 (a) G_t is C¹ (composition/product of C¹ maps), with DG_t(z)h = −|w|⁻¹ Dφ(z + tw)[h]·w. This is the rank-one map h ↦ a(h)·w with the linear form a := −|w|⁻¹ Dφ(z + tw), whose trace is a(w). Hence div G_t(z) = −|w|⁻¹ Dφ(z + tw)[w].
 (b) If G_t(z) ≠ 0 then φ(z + tw) ≠ 0. So tsupport G_t ⊆ tsupport(φ(· + tw)) = {z : z + tw ∈ tsupport φ} = tsupport φ − tw, a compact set (translation is a homeomorphism); hence G_t has compact support.
 (c) For z in that set, z + tw ∈ tsupport φ ⊆ B_R, so |z| ≤ |z + tw| + t|w| < R + |w| (as 0 ≤ t ≤ 1). Thus tsupport G_t ⊆ B_{R+|w|}.
 (d) |G_t(z)| = |w|⁻¹·|φ(z + tw)|·|w| = |φ(z + tw)| ≤ 1.
 By the hypothesis, ∫_F −|w|⁻¹ Dφ(z + tw)[w] dz ≤ C; multiplying by |w| > 0:
 (∗) ∫_F Dφ(z + tw)[w] dz ≥ −|w|·C for every t ∈ [0, 1].
3. (Differentiation under the integral sign.) Let Φ(t) := ∫_F φ(z + tw) dz for t ∈ ℝ. Dφ is continuous with compact support (tsupport Dφ ⊆ tsupport φ), so |Dφ| ≤ B for some B. Fix t₀ ∈ ℝ. For |t − t₀| < 1 the t-derivative of the integrand, Dφ(z + tw)[w] (chain rule), satisfies |Dφ(z + tw)[w]| ≤ B|w| and vanishes unless z + tw ∈ tsupport φ ⊆ B_R, which forces |z| < R + |t||w| ≤ R + (|t₀| + 1)|w|. Hence it is dominated by B|w|·1_{closedBall(0, R+(|t₀|+1)|w|)}(z), which is integrable on F. The integrands are continuous in z (so measurable), z ↦ φ(z + t₀w) is integrable (continuous, compact support), and z ↦ Dφ(z + t₀w)[w] is continuous. By the dominated differentiation theorem, Φ is differentiable at t₀ with Φ'(t₀) = ∫_F Dφ(z + t₀w)[w] dz.
4. Ψ(t) := Φ(t) + |w|·C·t is differentiable on ℝ with Ψ'(t) = Φ'(t) + |w|·C, which is ≥ 0 for t ∈ (0, 1) by (∗). Ψ is continuous on [0, 1] and differentiable in its interior with nonnegative derivative, so Ψ is monotone on [0, 1]; in particular Ψ(0) ≤ Ψ(1), i.e. Φ(0) − Φ(1) ≤ |w|·C.
5. φ and φ(· + w) are continuous with compact support, hence integrable on F, so Φ(0) − Φ(1) = ∫_F φ(z) dz − ∫_F φ(z + w) dz = ∫_F (φ(z) − φ(z + w)) dz. Together with 4 this is the claim. ∎

Parent proof step 3 ('{u_k|_{B_R} : k ∈ ℕ} is totally bounded in L¹(B_R)'), with step 1 supplied by mollify_l1 and step 2 by mollified_lipschitz and sup_net; total boundedness is expressed with centres taken from the sequence itself, in the form L((F_k Δ F_i) ∩ B_R) < θ. Notation: E := ℝ^{m+1}, L := L^{m+1}, B_r := B_r(0), u_k := 1_{F_k}.

1. Apply the hypothesis with radius R + 1 > 0: there are C ∈ ℝ and k₀ ∈ ℕ such that for every k ≥ k₀, ∫_{F_k} div g ≤ C for every C¹ compactly supported g with tsupport g ⊆ B_{R+1} and |g| ≤ 1. Taking k = k₀ and g = 0 gives C ≥ 0.
2. Let ε := min(1/2, θ/(3(C + 1))). Then 0 < ε ≤ 1 and ε·C ≤ θC/(3(C + 1)) < θ/3.
3. By mollifier (n = m + 1, r = ε) choose ρ : E → ℝ, C^∞ (hence C¹ and continuous), with compact support, ρ ≥ 0, ∫ ρ = 1 and support ρ ⊆ B_ε.
4. Put v_k(x) := ∫ ρ(y)·1_{F_k}(x − y) dy. For every k ≥ k₀, mollify_l1 (with F := F_k and these R, C, ε, ρ; its hypothesis is the bound of step 1) gives ∫_{B_R} |u_k − v_k| ≤ ε·C < θ/3.
5. By mollified_lipschitz there is L ∈ ℝ with |v_k(x)| ≤ L and |v_k(x) − v_k(x')| ≤ L|x − x'| for all k, x, x'. In particular each v_k is continuous (Lipschitz), hence Borel.
6. Let V := L(B_R) < ∞ and δ := θ/(3(V + 1)) > 0, so δ·V < θ/3. Apply sup_net to the compact K := closedBall(0, R), the functions g_j := v_{k₀+j} (j ∈ ℕ), the constant L (both hypotheses hold by 5) and δ: there is a finite S' ⊆ ℕ such that every j has i' ∈ S' with |v_{k₀+j}(x) − v_{k₀+i'}(x)| ≤ δ for all x ∈ K.
7. Let S := {0, 1, …, k₀ − 1} ∪ {k₀ + i' : i' ∈ S'}, a finite set. Let k ∈ ℕ. If k < k₀, take i := k ∈ S: F_k Δ F_k = ∅, so the measure is 0 < θ. If k ≥ k₀, apply 6 to j := k − k₀ and let i := k₀ + i' ∈ S; then k₀ + j = k, i ≥ k₀ and |v_k − v_i| ≤ δ on B_R ⊆ K.
8. Pointwise |u_k − u_i| ≤ |u_k − v_k| + |v_k − v_i| + |u_i − v_i|. All functions involved are Borel and bounded (|u| ≤ 1, |v| ≤ L), hence integrable on B_R (finite measure). Integrating over B_R and using 4 for k and for i (both ≥ k₀) and 6 (∫_{B_R} |v_k − v_i| ≤ δ·V): ∫_{B_R} |u_k − u_i| ≤ εC + δV + εC < θ/3 + θ/3 + θ/3 = θ.
9. |u_k − u_i| = 1_{F_k Δ F_i} pointwise, so ∫_{B_R} |u_k − u_i| = L((F_k Δ F_i) ∩ B_R), a finite number. Hence L((F_k Δ F_i) ∩ B_R) < θ (as extended reals: L(…) = ENNReal.ofReal(∫_{B_R} |u_k − u_i|) < ENNReal.ofReal θ). ∎

subproblems.title: Pigeonhole: infinite index sets of pairwise close sets
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and F_k ⊆ ℝⁿ (k ∈ ℕ) be sets such that for every R > 0 and θ > 0 there is a finite S ⊆ ℕ such that every k has some i ∈ S with L((F_k Δ F_i) ∩ B_R(0)) < θ. Then for every r ∈ ℕ and every infinite I ⊆ ℕ there is an infinite J ⊆ I with L((F_j Δ F_l) ∩ B_{r+1}(0)) ≤ 2^{−r} for all j, l ∈ J.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 4 ('every sequence in a totally bounded subset has a Cauchy … subsequence'): this is the pigeonhole step behind it, in the form required by the diagonal lemma (sibling diagonal_subseq). Measures are extended reals (ENNReal); no measurability is needed (only monotonicity and subadditivity of the outer measure).

1. Apply the hypothesis with R := r + 1 > 0 and θ := (1/2)^{r+1} > 0. This gives a finite S ⊆ ℕ and, choosing for each k one such i, a function c : ℕ → ℕ with c(k) ∈ S and L((F_k Δ F_{c(k)}) ∩ B_{r+1}) < ENNReal.ofReal((1/2)^{r+1}) = 2^{−(r+1)} for all k.
2. I ⊆ ⋃_{s∈S} (I ∩ c⁻¹({s})) because c(k) ∈ S for every k. If each of these finitely many sets were finite, their union, and hence I, would be finite. So there is s ∈ S such that J := I ∩ c⁻¹({s}) is infinite; clearly J ⊆ I.
3. Let j, l ∈ J, so c(j) = c(l) = s. Since F_j Δ F_l ⊆ (F_j Δ F_s) ∪ (F_s Δ F_l) and F_s Δ F_l = F_l Δ F_s, monotonicity and subadditivity give L((F_j Δ F_l) ∩ B_{r+1}) ≤ L((F_j Δ F_s) ∩ B_{r+1}) + L((F_l Δ F_s) ∩ B_{r+1}) ≤ 2^{−(r+1)} + 2^{−(r+1)} = 2^{−r}. ∎

subproblems.title: Diagonal extraction from nested infinite cliques
subproblems.statement: Let C : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop be any family of binary relations C r on ℕ. Suppose that for every r ∈ ℕ and every infinite set I ⊆ ℕ there is an infinite set J ⊆ I such that C r j l holds for all j, l ∈ J. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that C r (φ(r + 1)) (φ(r)) holds for every r ∈ ℕ.

Source. Parent proof steps 4–5 ('L¹(B_R) is complete … The limit is an indicator … F₀ := ⋃_N …, a Borel set with 1_{F₀} = w_N a.e. on B_N'). Specialized to a fast-Cauchy sequence of indicators, the L¹ limit is constructed directly as the indicator of the liminf set (this is the Riesz–Fischer completeness argument), which is Borel and serves all radii at once, so no L¹ spaces, a.e. subsequences or patching of representatives are needed. Measures are extended reals.

1. Define F₀ := ⋃_{J∈ℕ} ⋂_{i∈ℕ} G_{J+i}. It is Borel (countable unions and intersections of Borel sets).
2. Claim: for every j, G_j Δ F₀ ⊆ ⋃_{l∈ℕ} (G_{j+l+1} Δ G_{j+l}). Let x be outside the right side, i.e. x ∈ G_{j+l+1} ⟺ x ∈ G_{j+l} for every l. By induction on l, x ∈ G_{j+l} ⟺ x ∈ G_j for every l. If x ∈ G_j, then x ∈ ⋂_i G_{j+i} ⊆ F₀. If x ∈ F₀, then x ∈ ⋂_i G_{J+i} for some J; taking i := j gives x ∈ G_{J+j} = G_{j+J}, hence x ∈ G_j. So x ∈ G_j ⟺ x ∈ F₀, i.e. x ∉ G_j Δ F₀.
3. Fix R ∈ ℝ and let N := ⌈R⌉₊ (natural-number ceiling), so R ≤ N. For j ≥ N and every l: R ≤ N ≤ j + l < j + l + 1, hence B_R(0) ⊆ B_{j+l+1}(0). By 2, monotonicity and countable subadditivity: L((G_j Δ F₀) ∩ B_R(0)) ≤ Σ_l L((G_{j+l+1} Δ G_{j+l}) ∩ B_{(j+l)+1}(0)) ≤ Σ_l 2^{−(j+l)} = 2^{−j}·Σ_l 2^{−l} = 2^{−j}·2.
4. 2·2^{−j} → 0 as j → ∞ (geometric sequence with ratio 1/2 < 1 times the finite constant 2), and the measures are ≥ 0; by the squeeze theorem (the upper bound holding for j ≥ N), L((G_j Δ F₀) ∩ B_R(0)) → 0. This holds for every R ∈ ℝ (for R ≤ 0 the ball is empty and the argument is unchanged). ∎
